name: protondrive-cli-connection
description: Connect to ProtonDrive via CLI for cloud storage access and file operations
steps: Install rclone: check with 'which rclone' or install
Configure: run 'rclone config' and select ProtonDrive
Authenticate: complete browser-based OAuth flow
Verify: run 'rclone about protondrive:' to check connection
Use: 'rclone ls protondrive:' to browse files
Mount (optional): 'rclone mount protondrive: ~/mnt/proton'
examples: rclone ls protondrive:
rclone copy ~/local/file.txt protondrive:/backups/
rclone sync ~/Projects protondrive:/projects-backup

name: github-ssh-authentication
description: Connect to GitHub via SSH for push/pull operations without password prompts
steps: Generate SSH key: 'ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C email'
Add to ssh-agent: 'eval $(ssh-agent -s)' then 'ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519'
Copy public key: 'cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub'
Add to GitHub: Settings > SSH and GPG keys > New SSH key
Test connection: 'ssh -T git@github.com'
Clone repos with SSH: 'git clone git@github.com:user/repo.git'
examples: git push origin main
git clone git@github.com:AR-Davis/prima_distributed_local.git
ssh -T git@github.com

name: codeberg-ssh-authentication
description: Connect to Codeberg via SSH for repository operations and upstream syncs
steps: Use existing SSH key or generate new: 'ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C email'
Add public key to Codeberg: Settings > SSH/GPG Keys > Add Key
Test connection: 'ssh -T git@codeberg.org'
Clone with SSH: 'git clone git@codeberg.org:user/repo.git'
For upstream: 'git remote add upstream git@codeberg.org:kinch_kesh/localize_it.git'
examples: git push codeberg main
git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/main

name: tailscale-mesh-connection
description: Connect device to Grove Tailscale mesh for secure inter-device communication
steps: Install Tailscale: 'curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh'
Authenticate: 'sudo tailscale up' and complete browser login
Verify: 'tailscale status' to see mesh nodes
Check IP: 'tailscale ip -4' for your Tailnet address
Access other nodes: ping or SSH using 100.x.x.x addresses
examples: tailscale status
tailscale ping myceliumnetwork

name: syncthing-folder-sync
description: Set up Syncthing for bidirectional folder sync across Grove devices
steps: Install Syncthing: 'sudo apt install syncthing' or download
Enable service: 'systemctl --user enable syncthing'
Start service: 'systemctl --user start syncthing'
Access web UI: http://127.0.0.1:8384
Add device: Share device ID with mesh, accept shares
Add folder: Set path, select devices to share with
Verify sync: Check folder status in web UI
examples: grove-commons folder to Pixel 2
projects folder sync to TheTower
vault backup to Coven

name: grove-delegation-workflow
description: How Kinch delegates work among Grove members based on task type, expertise, and current capacity
steps: Identify task type: Research, Code/Review, Trading, Verification, Infrastructure, Documentation
Match to Grove member expertise: Newton for deep research, Programmer for code review, Budger for trading, etc.
Check member WAKE.md or status for current capacity and blockers
Formulate clear task with context, acceptance criteria, and deadline
Delegate via appropriate channel: subagent for hounds, direct message for humans, Grove Commons for async
Track in Corraler/Pupper or project-pulse.log for accountability
Follow up if no response within deadline window
triggers: Shepherd overflow - too many parallel streams
examples: Code review: Delegate to Programmer with security focus
Research task: Delegate to Newton with Feynman + ELI5 skills
Trading analysis: Delegate to Budger with AEGS parameters
Status check: Delegate to Pupper for weekly hound roundup
Verification: Delegate to Tracker for contact/source confirmation

name: newton-deep-research
description: Deep research workflow using Feynman technique and ELI5 simplification for complex technical topics
steps: Receive research question from user
Apply Feynman technique: break into fundamental concepts
Research technical sources (papers, docs, code)
Create ELI5 summary for accessibility
Provide technical deep-dive for detail
Document findings in ~/grove-commons/RESEARCH/ or project-pulse.log
examples: Research distributed LLM inference across home network devices
Explain RPC tensor padding and why it matters for quantized models
Deep dive into Prima.cpp architecture and Halda algorithm
Research Alpaca backtesting skill limitations for 0DTE options

name: eli5-technical-explanation
description: Simplify complex technical concepts using everyday analogies and progressive disclosure
steps: Identify the core concept to explain
Find everyday analogy (car engine, plumbing, etc.)
Explain the 'why' before the 'how'
Use progressive disclosure: simple first, details on demand
Verify understanding with check questions
Provide deep-dive reference for advanced readers
triggers: how does Y work in simple terms?
examples: RPC tensor padding is like... making sure puzzle pieces fit even if they're odd sizes
Distributed inference is like... dividing a book among friends to read faster
LoRA fine-tuning is like... learning to drive a new car without forgetting how to ride a bike

name: comparative-analysis-research
description: Research and compare multiple options, technologies, or approaches with structured analysis
steps: Define comparison criteria (features, compatibility, cost, etc.)
Research each option independently
Create comparison matrix
Analyze trade-offs and edge cases
Provide recommendation with justification
Document decision rationale for future reference
examples: GrapheneOS vs DivestOS: security, compatibility, maintenance
Tailscale vs ZeroTier: mesh VPN comparison
llama.cpp vs vLLM: inference engine evaluation

name: memory-palace-tool-organization
description: Organize AI tools and capabilities using personas (memory palace / theater of mind) for terminal-native workflows without GUI dependency
steps: Identify tool domains (research, code, fiscal, investigation, etc.)
Assign breed archetypes to each domain (Bloodhound for tracking, Pointer for research, etc.)
Create persona files with unique voice, skills, and memory anchors
Store in accessible location (e.g., ~/.pi/personas/{name}/)
Create WAKE files for current status and quick orientation
Summon by name for domain-specific tasks
Cross-reference personas for complex multi-domain work
examples: Newton (Pointer) for research — remember by 'points to knowledge'
Tracker (Coonhound) for investigation — remember by 'follows the scent'
Budger (Bloodhound) for trading — remember by 'tracks finance'
Wake up Newton — loads research context and arXiv capabilities
Wake up Tracker — loads OSINT databases and investigation pathways

name: online-offline-pack-architecture
description: Split AI capabilities into online and offline packs with clear handoff protocols for connectivity continuity
steps: Identify which capabilities require internet (APIs, cloud services, real-time data)
Identify which capabilities work locally (file search, local LLM, mesh networking)
Assign hounds to online pack (cloud-connected) or offline pack (local-first)
Create hybrid hounds for tasks that bridge both (scheduling, task queuing)
Design handoff protocols for transitions (online→offline, offline→online)
Establish surrogate roles (e.g., offline hound replaces online hound when disconnected)
Document connectivity requirements for each capability
examples: Online: Newton (arXiv), Tracker (OSINT databases), Budger (Alpaca API)
Offline: Toby (local files), Builder (mesh), Pupper (local LLM)
Hybrid: Corraler (queues online tasks, runs offline tasks always)
Surrogate: Pupper replaces Shepherd when offline
Handoff: Newton research flows to Toby for offline access

name: confidence-scored-pattern-detection
description: Add confidence scores to pattern detection to reduce false positives and identify reliable training patterns
steps: Define confidence calculation function (0.0-1.0) based on keyword strength, context, specificity
Set confidence threshold (e.g., ≥0.3) for pattern inclusion
Calculate confidence per pattern instance
Categorize into levels: high (≥0.7), medium (0.5-0.7), low (<0.5)
Generate statistics: avg confidence, distribution per pattern type
Filter to reliable patterns (≥0.5) for training data
Report recommendations: which patterns are trustworthy
triggers: high false positive rate in pattern detection
need to identify reliable patterns for training
shadow analysis producing too much noise
examples: 'Write Python function' → code_requests @ 0.80 (high confidence)
'Hi' → explain_requests @ 0.10 (filtered out, below threshold)
'What is machine learning' → explain_requests @ 0.60 (medium, review before training)
Statistics: 45 high-confidence, 30 medium, 25 low (filtered)
